1.why: Density is mass divided by volume, so ρ = m ÷ V.

wrong.a: Multiplying mass and volume is not density.
wrong.c: Volume divided by mass is the inverse of density.
wrong.d: Adding mass and volume does not give density.

2.why: PM2.5 particles are tiny pollutants smaller than 2.5 micrometres.

wrong.b: Raindrops are much larger than PM2.5.
wrong.c: Clouds are water droplets, not PM2.5 particles.
wrong.d: Wind speed is measured in m/s, not particle size.

3.why: Trees and parks help filter air and reduce particle pollution.

wrong.a: More traffic adds more exhaust particles.
wrong.d: Dark asphalt does not clean the air.

_quiz_pool.question: What does ρ stand for in density equations?
_quiz_pool.explanation: ρ stands for density, representing mass per unit volume.

_quiz_pool.question: Which particles are known as PM2.5?
_quiz_pool.explanation: PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometres.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of density in SI?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Density is measured in kilograms per cubic metre (kg/m³).

_quiz_pool.question: If mass doubles while volume stays the same, density…
_quiz_pool.explanation: Density is directly proportional to mass.

_quiz_pool.question: Why do calm winds cause hazy air?
options: Particles stay close to the ground
_quiz_pool.explanation: Without wind to disperse them, pollutants accumulate near the surface.

_quiz_pool.question: Which action helps improve air quality?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Trees and plants help absorb pollutants and clean the air.

must_show: two clean white plates or bowls
one plate left outside and one inside for 24 hours
comparing dust or particle spots on both plates
safety: no flame, no chemicals, only household dust observation

story.title: Smoky days in the busy city
story.lead: Weather reports noted hazy skies and particle pollution in city areas [1]. Tiny air pollutants can travel far and affect people's breathing [2].
stat.1.label: air volume tested
stat.2.label: mass of PM2.5 particles
stat.3.label: particle concentration
story.body_1: Air quality changes when smoke, dust and exhaust mix into the air [1]. These tiny solid and liquid particles are called aerosols or particulate matter. When winds are calm, particles stay close to the ground where people walk and breathe every day [2].
story.body_2: Children and older people are most sensitive to bad air [3]. Planting trees, using public transport, and checking air quality reports help communities protect health and reduce pollution [2].
timeline.1.text: Traffic and morning activities release smoke and dust into the air.
timeline.2.text: Sunlight warms the air, but trapped particles create a hazy layer.
timeline.3.text: Cooler night air keeps particles close to the ground surface.
physics.title: Density of air and particles
physics.body_1: To understand how thick polluted air is, we look at density. Density tells us how much mass is packed into a given volume of space.
physics.body_2: We calculate density with mass divided by volume. A bigger mass in the same volume means higher density and thicker pollution.
physics.assumptions: We assume particles are spread evenly through the air volume.
